title: Q2 Results 13th Oct Live: Q2 Results Today Live: Tata Elxsi, ICICI Pru Life, Hero Motors shares trade mixed; PNB Gilts jumps 8% - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Q2 Results Today, 13th October 2026 Live Updates: Find all the latest Q2 results 2026 updates of Anand Rathi Share And Stock Brokers, Blue Pearl Agriventures, Den Networks, Dharti Proteins, Eimco Elecon (India), GTPL Hathway, Hero Motors, ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company, IGC Industries, International Travel House-$, Mapro Industries, Mudra Financial Services, Mukta Agriculture, PNB Gilts, Sejal Glass, Shree Krishna Infrastructure, SS Retail, State Trading Corporation of India, Talwalkars Better Value Fitness, Transformers and Rectifiers (India), Tata Elxsi and TRF

Transformers and Rectifiers (India) Limited (TARIL) reported a sharp jump in profitability for the July–September 2026 quarter, with standalone net profit surging 338 per cent year-on-year to ₹75 crore, driven by higher capacity utilisation and operating leverage across its Gujarat manufacturing plants.

Revenue from operations rose 66 per cent year-on-year to ₹709 crore in Q2FY27, while EBITDA nearly tripled to ₹114 crore, expanding the margin to 16.1 per cent from 8.7 per cent in the same quarter last year. For the half-year ended September 30, 2026, revenue grew 35 per cent to ₹1,268 crore and PAT rose 62 per cent to ₹125 crore.

The company’s un-executed order book stood at ₹7,237 crore as of September 30, 2026, up 32 per cent from ₹5,472 crore a year earlier, with 83 per cent of orders from power transformers. New order inflows during H1FY27 totalled ₹3,283 crore, a 161 per cent increase year-on-year. TARIL also disclosed a bid pipeline of ₹21,000 crore under active negotiation.

Notable orders secured during the quarter include the company’s first-ever nuclear sector contract, supplying generator transformers for NPCIL’s Kaiga Units 5 and 6, along with orders from APTRANSCO, Damodar Valley Corporation, Megha Engineering, and GETCO.

Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 25 per cent revenue growth, a 16 per cent EBITDA margin, and a PAT margin of 9–10 per cent. Commercial commissioning of backward integration facilities is targeted for Q1FY28.

ICICI Life Insurance Limited, formerly known as ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited, reported a strong set of numbers for the first half of FY2027, with Value of New Business (VNB) rising 22.3 per cent year-on-year to ₹12.83 billion and VNB margin expanding to 26 per cent, up from 24.7 per cent in full-year FY2026.

Profit after tax for the period grew 26.5 per cent to ₹7.60 billion. Annualised Premium Equivalent (APE) rose 15.1 per cent to ₹49.35 billion, while total premium income climbed 15.3 per cent to ₹245.05 billion. New business premium grew 25 per cent during the half-year period.

The results were accompanied by the company’s rebranding, dropping “Prudential” from its name. Management said the new name reflects its standalone identity while retaining the ICICI franchise’s trust and legacy. Core operations, strategy, and governance remain unchanged.

Protection remained the fastest-growing segment, with Protection APE surging 39.5 per cent to ₹11.55 billion. Retail sum assured jumped 34.9 per cent to ₹2,315.21 billion. The company’s 13-month persistency ratio held at 84.5 per cent as of September 30, 2026.

Embedded value grew 12.2 per cent year-on-year to ₹566.69 billion. Assets under management stood at ₹3,289.64 billion. The solvency ratio was 229.9 per cent, comfortably above regulatory requirements. The individual death claims settlement ratio remained at 99.3 per cent, unchanged from H1-FY2026.

Eimco Elecon (India) Limited on Tuesday reported a sharp jump in revenue and profits for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, even as the company disclosed the resignation of its Chief Financial Officer.

Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 rose 70.9 per cent year-on-year to ₹57 crore from ₹33 crore in the same quarter last year. EBITDA more than doubled, growing 108.8 per cent to ₹11 crore, with margins expanding to 18.8 per cent from 15.4 per cent. Profit after tax climbed 46.5 per cent to ₹8 crore for the quarter. For the first half of FY27, revenue grew 33.3 per cent to ₹134 crore, while PAT rose 17.1 per cent to ₹23 crore with a margin of 17.3 per cent.

The order book as of September 30, 2026 stood at ₹133 crore, a 202 per cent increase from ₹44 crore a year earlier, signalling strong near-term revenue visibility for the Vallabh Vidyanagar-based mining equipment maker.

Separately, the board noted the resignation of Vishal C. Begwani as CFO and Key Managerial Personnel, effective close of business on October 30, 2026. Begwani, who submitted his resignation on September 5, cited a professional opportunity outside the organisation.

PNB Gilts Limited on Tuesday reported a net profit of ₹125.53 crore for the first half of FY 2026-27 (April–September 2026), with profit before tax at ₹168.49 crore. Earnings per share for the six-month period stood at ₹6.98.

However, the quarter-on-quarter performance showed a sharp drop. For Q2 FY27 (July–September 2026), the company posted a profit after tax of ₹44.84 crore, down roughly 45 per cent from ₹80.70 crore in Q1 FY27. Profit before tax for Q2 came in at ₹60.24 crore against ₹108.26 crore the previous quarter. The company had reported a loss in the same quarter of the prior year.

The sequential decline was driven by a net loss on fair value changes of ₹17.71 crore in Q2, compared to a gain of ₹18.23 crore in Q1, reflecting bond market volatility. Finance costs remained elevated at ₹34,216 crore for the quarter.

Net interest income for H1 FY27 stood at ₹194.86 crore. Total income for the half-year was ₹87,360 crore.

PNB Gilts is India’s only listed standalone Primary Dealer and a subsidiary of Punjab National Bank.
